However, this equivalence assumes the GNN uses the "complete" version of these PEs, which requires $O(n^3)$ time and space complexity. Instead, practitioners commonly use truncated variants of these encodings, such as the first $k$ eigenspaces or powers of the adjacency matrix. However, the theoretical properties of these truncated PEs are unknown. In this work, we initiate the study of these truncated PEs. Theoretically, we show that, under truncation, several families of PEs are fundamentally different in expressive power. As a corollary, we show that truncated spectral PEs are no longer stronger than the 1-WL test. We also study a family of spectral PEs, the $k$-harmonic distances, to highlight the differences in expressive power of even closely related truncated PEs. Finally, we experimentally show that a mix of truncated PEs is preferable to any single family on real-world datasets.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates truncated positional encodings (PEs) in graph neural networks (GNNs), revealing differences in their expressive power compared to complete versions.
AI.motivation: To explore the theoretical properties of truncated positional encodings in graph neural networks, as current literature primarily focuses on complete encodings.
AI.method: The authors theoretically analyze truncated versions of spectral and walk-based PEs, comparing their expressive power and conducting experiments on real-world datasets.
AI.result: It is shown that truncated spectral PEs are equivalent to the 1-WL test, and that different truncated PEs exhibit fundamentally different expressiveness; a combination of truncated PEs outperforms singular families.
AI.conclusion: Truncated PEs should be studied further due to their varied properties, and a mixed approach in using them can enhance performance in GNNs.

title: Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates: On the Sparsity and Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
summary: On-policy distillation (\textsc{OPD}) has recently become a prominent post-training recipe as it combines two desirable ingredients: on-policy student trajectories and dense teacher supervision, yet how this hybrid changes a model's parameters remains unclear. Across several language and vision-language model pairs and use cases, our analysis yields two main findings. On sparsity, \textsc{OPD}-style updates are small and coordinate-sparse. They are distributed across layers and are usually FFN-heavy. This sparse structure is operationally useful: training only the discovered subnetwork recovers nearly the same performance as full \textsc{OPD}. However, the sparsity-inducing SGD optimizer underperforms AdamW in our optimizer ablation, likely because dense teacher supervision preserves heterogeneous coordinate-wise gradient scales where AdamW's adaptive scaling remains useful. On geometry, the updates are numerically full-rank but spectrally concentrated; they lie mostly away from the principal singular subspaces of the source weights and fall disproportionately on coordinates where the source weights are close to zero. These findings suggest that dense teacher supervision does not turn \textsc{OPD} into ordinary dense parameter rewriting; instead, \textsc{OPD} retains important geometric signatures of on-policy post-training.

AI.tldr: On-policy distillation (OPD) reveals small, coordinate-sparse updates across layers, mainly in FFNs, achieving similar performance to full OPD with a subnetwork. The sparsity-inducing SGD optimizer has limitations compared to AdamW, while the updates are full-rank, concentrated away from main weight subspaces, indicating geometric preservation in OPD without typical dense rewriting.
AI.motivation: To explore how on-policy distillation (OPD) influences model parameters and structures, especially concerning the effects of sparse updates and dense teacher supervision in language and vision-language models.
AI.method: The study involves analyzing OPD across various model pairs, focusing on the characteristics of updates in terms of sparsity and geometric distribution, while comparing different optimization strategies.
AI.result: Findings indicate that OPD updates are sparsely distributed, primarily in feedforward networks, with training on a subnetwork yielding nearly equivalent performance to full OPD. The optimizer choices show that AdamW outperforms sparsity-inducing SGD.
AI.conclusion: Dense teacher supervision in OPD preserves geometric properties during updates, differentiating it from standard dense parameter rewriting and highlighting the significance of on-policy post-training effects.
